'''Martin Schröder''' is a British chemist who is a Research Professor of Chemistry<ref name=epmc>{{EuropePMC}}</ref><ref name=gs/> who served as [[Vice President]] and [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of the Faculty of Science and Engineering at the [[University of Manchester]] from 2015 to 2025.<ref name=vicedeanery>{{cite web|author=Anon|url=http://www.manchester.ac.uk/discover/news/article/?id=14095|year=2015|title=New Vice-President and Dean for EPS faculty|website=manchester.ac.uk}}</ref> He also served as Executive Dean of the Faculty of Science from 2011 to 2015 and Professor of Inorganic Chemistry at the [[University of Nottingham]] from 1995 to 2015.<ref name=official>{{Official URL}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Martin Schröder was born in [[Taplow]], [[Buckinghamshire]] of [[Estonia]]n [[refugee]] parents in 1954,<ref name=dob>GRO Register of Births: JUN 1954 6a 541 ETON - Martin Schröder, mmn = Kruus'na</ref> and was educated at Montem Primary School and [[Slough Grammar School]]. He is first in family to attend university, and was awarded a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] degree in chemistry from the [[University of Sheffield]] in 1975 and a [[PhD]] from [[Imperial College London|Imperial College of Science, Technology and Medicine, London]] in 1978 where his research on oxo complexes of [[osmium]] and [[ruthenium]] was supervised by William P. Griffith.<ref name=mphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=Imperial College London (University of London)|url=https://catalogue.libraries.london.ac.uk/record=b3009176~S1|hdl=10044/1/8148|title=Reactions of oxo complexes of osmium and ruthenium|first= Martin|last=Schröder|date=1978|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.471806}}|website=london.ac.uk|oclc=500557068}} {{free access}}</ref>

==Career==

After [[postdoctoral fellow]]ships at the ETH, Zürich with [[Albert Eschenmoser]],<ref name=personalpage>{{cite web|url=https://research.manchester.ac.uk/en/persons/martin-schr%C3%B6der/|author=University of Manchester|year=2025|title=Prof. Martin Schröder|website=manchester.ac.uk}}</ref> funded by a Royal Society-Swiss National Foundation Fellowship, and at the [[University of Cambridge]] with [[Jack Lewis, Baron Lewis of Newnham|Lord Lewis of Newnham]],<ref name=personalpage>{{cite web|url=https://research.manchester.ac.uk/en/persons/martin-schr%C3%B6der/|author=University of Manchester|year=2025|title=Prof. Martin Schröder|website=manchester.ac.uk}}</ref> he was appointed to a senior demonstratorship at the University of Edinburgh in 1982.<ref name=personalpage>{{cite web|url=https://research.manchester.ac.uk/en/persons/martin-schr%C3%B6der/|author=University of Manchester|year=2025|title=Prof. Martin Schröder|website=manchester.ac.uk}}</ref> He was subsequently promoted to Lecturer, Reader and then Professor, and in 1995 was appointed to the University of Nottingham as Head and Professor of Inorganic Chemistry. He served as head of the School of Chemistry at the University of Nottingham from 1999 to 2005,<ref>{{cite web|author=Anon|year=2013|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130716131822/http://www.nottingham.ac.uk/chemistry/people/m.schroder|url=http://www.nottingham.ac.uk/chemistry/people/m.schroder|archivedate=2013-07-16|title=Martin Schroder at the University of Nottingham|website=nottingham.ac.uk|publisher=University of Nottingham}}</ref> and as Executive Dean of the Faculty of Science (2011–2015). In 2015 he moved to the [[University of Manchester]] as Vice-President and Dean of the Faculty of Science and Engineering and Professor of Chemistry.<ref name=personalpage>{{cite web|url=https://research.manchester.ac.uk/en/persons/martin-schr%C3%B6der/|author=University of Manchester|year=2025|title=Prof. Martin Schröder|website=manchester.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name=Henry>{{cite web|url=https://www.royce.ac.uk/our-people/martin-schroder/|author=Henry Royce Institute|year=2025|title=Professor Martin Schröder|website=manchester.ac.uk}}</ref>

Schröder has been a visiting professor at the University of Toronto, Canada, the University of Otago, Dunedin, New Zealand, and the Université Louis Pasteur, Strasbourg, France.<ref name=personalpage>{{cite web|url=https://research.manchester.ac.uk/en/persons/martin-schr%C3%B6der/|author=University of Manchester|year=2025|title=Prof. Martin Schröder|website=manchester.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name=UKRI>{{cite web|url=https://www.ukri.org/people/martin-schroder/|author=UK Research and Innovation|year=2023|title=Professor Martin Schröder|website=ukri.org}}</ref> He has published over 600 publications and patents.<ref name=ORCID>{{cite web|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6992-0700|year=2026|title=Martin Schroder|website=orcid.org}}</ref> His early independent research focussed on the chemistry of transition metal thioether and aza macrocyclic complexes with particular focus on the stabilisation of unusual oxidation state species. This work led to the isolation and characterisation of unique mononuclear M(I)/(III) (M = Ni, Pd, Pt) and M(II) (M = Ag, Au, Rh, Ir) complexes. His current research focuses on the development of new advanced functional materials, particularly metal-organic framework materials for selective fuel and toxic gas capture, purification and catalysis.<ref name=personalpage>{{cite web|url=https://research.manchester.ac.uk/en/persons/martin-schr%C3%B6der/|author=University of Manchester|year=2025|title=Prof. Martin Schröder|website=manchester.ac.uk}}</ref>He is currently (since 2021) a Member of Council of the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://epsrc.ukri.org/about/people/martin-schroeder1/|title=Martin Schröder|website=epsrc.ukri.org|publisher=[[UK Research and Innovation]]|access-date=11 August 2021|archive-date=11 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210811080749/https://epsrc.ukri.org/about/people/martin-schroeder1/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Controversy==
In 2021, Schröder sent an email to [[Christopher Jackson (geologist)|Christopher Jackson]] in his capacity as a Vice President of the University of Manchester, linking to a right wing website [[GB News]] and disputing the presence of [[institutional racism]] at the University of Manchester.<ref name=nature>{{cite journal|journal=Nature|doi=10.1038/d41586-022-03265-8|first=Tosin |last=Thompson|year=2022|title=The geoscientist fighting for universities to confront systemic racism: Christopher Jackson felt obligated to speak out against racism in UK institutions, but a lack of support left him disillusioned with academia|volume=610 |issue=7932 |pages=436–437 |pmid=36261560 |s2cid=252996516 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=racist>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220607093053/https://researchprofessionalnews.com/rr-news-uk-universities-2022-6-manchester-vice-president-told-to-apologise-over-racism-row/|archivedate=2022-06-07|url=https://researchprofessionalnews.com/rr-news-uk-universities-2022-6-manchester-vice-president-told-to-apologise-over-racism-row/|website=researchprofessionalnews.com|year=2022|first=Sophie|last=Inge|title=Manchester vice-president told to apologise over racism row}}</ref> Jackson has subsequently left the institution,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mancunion.com/2022/11/25/christopher-jackson-leaves-the-university-of-manchester-following-racism-row/|website=mancunion.com|title=Christopher Jackson leaves the University of Manchester following racism row|first=Nuura|last=Ahmed|year=2022|publisher=[[The Mancunion]]}}</ref> and Schröder has declined to apologise.

==Awards and honours==
In 1994 he was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] (FRSE) and [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]] (FRSC), and in 2016 he was elected [[Member of Academia Europaea]] (MAE). He has been a recipient of a Royal Society of Edinburgh Support Research Fellowship (1991/92), a Leverhulme Trust Senior Research Fellowship (2005/6), and a Royal Society Wolfson Merit Award (2005-2010). He has been awarded Honorary Degrees from Tallinn Technical University and from Nikolaev Institute of Inorganic Chemistry, Russian Academy of Sciences.<ref name=UKRI>{{cite web|url=https://www.ukri.org/people/martin-schroder/|author=UK Research and Innovation|year=2023|title=Professor Martin Schröder|website=ukri.org}}</ref>

Martin Schröder has been awarded Royal Society of Chemistry awards and prizes including:

Corday-Morgan Medal and Prize (1991)<br>
Tilden Lectureship and Medal (2001)<br>
Award for Chemistry of Transition Metals (2003)<br>
Award for Chemistry of the Noble Metals and their Compounds (2008)<br>
Nyholm Prize for Inorganic Chemistry (2020)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Martin Schröder, Nyholm Prize for Inorganic Chemistry winner 2020|url=https://www.rsc.org/awards-funding/awards/2020-winners/professor-martin-schroder/|access-date=2020-12-16|website=rsc.org|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry|language=en-GB}}</ref><br>
Dalton Horizon Prize for Functional Framework Materials: Design and Characterisation (2024)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Winner: 2024 Dalton Horizon Prize Functional Framework Materials: Design and Characterisation Team|url=https://www.rsc.org/standards-and-recognition/prizes/winners/functional-framework-materials-design-and-characterisation-team|access-date=2020-12-16|website=rsc.org|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry|language=en-GB}}</ref>
